title: Hall v. Hall (2018)
summary: Consolidated actions retained separate identities for finality and appealability.
notes:
Source-limited note account. The underlying parties’ personal dispute and the complete procedural history are not reproduced in the assigned note.

Facts: Ethlyn Hall sued her son Samuel over his handling of her Virgin Islands property (the 'trust case'), her daughter Elsa succeeded her as trustee and plaintiff, Samuel sued Elsa individually, and the cases were consolidated under Rule 42(a) and tried together; the Third Circuit dismissed Elsa's appeal from the judgment in the individual case as premature, and the Supreme Court (Roberts, C.J., unanimous) reversed, holding that a final judgment in one consolidated case is immediately appealable.

sections.Parties: The parties litigated separate civil actions that were consolidated in one court.
sections.Material Facts: The procedural issue arose because consolidation brought actions together for administration while a judgment resolved an independently filed action. The casebook note supplies the consolidation issue but does not reproduce the full underlying factual controversy.
sections.Procedural History: The Supreme Court held that the consolidated cases retained their independence for the finality and appealability question.
sections.Issue: Did consolidation make the separate cases a single action for purposes of finality and appeal?
sections.Holding: No. The cases retained their independent identity for that purpose.
sections.Reasoning: The chapter places Hall alongside the principle that consolidation serves convenience and efficient administration without automatically changing the parties’ substantive rights or making a party in one suit a party in another. The implication is limited to the legal consequence being evaluated, rather than a claim that consolidation has no procedural effects.

learning.why: Consolidated actions retained separate identities for finality and appealability.

topics.cp-separate-trials: Consolidation did not merge the independent actions for finality and appealability.
topics.cp-mdl: The chapter uses the separate-identity principle when explaining coordinated proceedings.
topics.cp-frcp-42: The holding construes consolidation under Rule 42(a).
topics.cp-finality: The case decides when a judgment in a consolidated action is final for appeal under § 1291.
